s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic abdominal discomfort with worsening diarrhea and generalized weakness
salient_findings: Green-brown slimy stools multiple times per day
Diffuse colonic wall thickening with pericolonic stranding on abdominal CT
Intensely fludeoxyglucose-avid focus in the left anterior pelvis on PET scan
key_facts: 92-year-old woman with hyperlipidemia and pulmonary sarcoidosis
Previously treated with steroids
Internal hemorrhoids
1-week history of worsening diarrhea and abdominal discomfort
Poor appetite and generalized weakness
Last colonoscopy at age 80 was unremarkable
Hospitalized for rectal bleeding 9 months earlier
Abdominal CT showed left-sided colitis and possible diverticulitis
PET scan showed intensely fludeoxyglucose-avid focus in the left anterior pelvis
Temperature 98.8°F, heart rate 80 bpm, and blood pressure 102/70 mm Hg on admission
White blood cell count 9.8 K/μL, hemoglobin 12 g/dL, and C-reactive protein 27.0 mg/dL
Fecal calprotectin 2562.8 μg/g and carcinoembryonic antigen 1.7
Stool tests for bacterial culture, PCR, Clostridioides difficile, ova and parasites, and leukocytes were negative

shortlist.label: Colorectal cancer
shortlist.why_kept: Intensely fludeoxyglucose-avid focus on PET scan and diffuse colonic wall thickening on abdominal CT

shortlist.label: Ulcerative colitis
shortlist.why_kept: Worsening diarrhea, abdominal discomfort, and elevated fecal calprotectin

shortlist.label: Diverticulitis
shortlist.why_kept: Previous abdominal CT showing possible diverticulitis and current symptoms of diarrhea and abdominal discomfort

shortlist.label: Crohn's disease
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic abdominal discomfort, worsening diarrhea, and elevated inflammatory markers

shortlist.label: Ischemic colitis
shortlist.why_kept: Abdominal CT showing diffuse colonic wall thickening and patient's age increasing risk for ischemic events

raw.rationale: The patient's history of rectal bleeding, left-sided colitis, and a PET scan showing an intensely fludeoxyglucose-avid focus in the left anterior pelvis are highly suggestive of malignancy, and the elevated fecal calprotectin and carcinoembryonic antigen levels support this diagnosis

rejected.label: Ulcerative colitis
rejected.why: While the patient has colitis, the presence of a mass and the PET scan findings are more indicative of cancer

rejected.label: Diverticulitis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings are not typical of diverticulitis, and the PET scan suggests a malignant process

rejected.label: Crohn's disease
rejected.why: The patient's age and lack of prior inflammatory bowel disease symptoms make Crohn's disease less likely, and the imaging findings are more suggestive of cancer

rejected.label: Ischemic colitis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings do not suggest ischemia, and the PET scan findings are more indicative of malignancy
